03 — About

Behavior is the interface.

Background

I’m Jack. I studied psychology and sociology, and by my senior year I’d noticed that the questions I cared about (why people do what they do, and what gets in their way) are the same ones a good product has to answer. So after graduating I trained in UX research and design and started working with real clients.

How I work

I start with people, not screens: interviews, surveys, card sorts, journey maps and usability tests. The evidence decides what gets designed, whether that’s a support site, an app’s filters, or a service that happens mostly in person.

Accessibility matters to me personally. My grandmother has macular degeneration, so I’ve seen how quickly the web gets harder when a design assumes perfect eyesight, and I design with that in mind.

What I’m looking for

A UX research role, or a research-heavy design role, on a team that builds with its users instead of guessing about them. I want to go deep on research first and grow into design from there, helping companies make digital and in-person experiences that are intuitive, connected and accessible.
